meta.title: Can we trust acquisition-channel conclusions when source values are missing?
meta.question: Assess the effect of missing acquisition source on channel conclusions.
meta.author: Codex

items: Check numbers refer to individual JSONL query logs in this folder.
Unknown is an unallocated first-touch source; hypothetical reassignment is a sensitivity bound, not a correction.
Signup
One registered user counted in the UTC month of signup.
New payer
A user counted in the month of their first successful charge, by their recorded acquisition source.
MAU
Distinct identified users active in a UTC month.

blocks.text: Qualified yes for large descriptive differences in this fixture: missing sources are approximately 1% of signups, and the example channel shift remains large under extreme reassignment. This does not establish that recorded sources are correct or that marketing caused the outcomes.

items: Across April-September, 135 of 13,600 signups (0.99%) have unknown source. Monthly unknown share ranges from 0.98% to 1.01% (checks 5 and 10).
In July, paid social has 1,582 signups versus 453 organic; allocating all 25 unknown signups to organic still leaves social ahead by 1,104 (check 14).
The database build registry hash differs from the current repository registry hash; verify the precise definition changes before relying on Gold for consequential decisions (check 4 and run notes).

rows: Complete UTC months [2026-04-01, 2026-10-01); monthly signup and first-payment event counts.
Supporting metrics v1.1; MAU v1.1. Source is the fixed first-touch user label. Unknown remains separate. Same-month CAC is spend divided by first-time payers in the month, not cohort CAC.
Gold marketing and activity marts for compatible monthly aggregates, Silver profile for checks, Bronze users for raw values.
Succeeded 2026-11-09; build-time reconciliation passed. Recorded source fingerprints have not been recomputed. Snapshot is metadata, not a verified hash.

items: Baseline: inventory layers, build, population, unknown labels and monthly segment counts (checks 1-13).
Round 1: test whether unknown attribution is material; whether it can overturn illustrative channel comparisons; and whether recorded source proves causal attribution (checks 5, 10, 14).
Stopped after one round: illustrative sensitivity is bounded; label accuracy and causality cannot be established from these fields alone.

rows: Unknown signups / total; unknown active / MAU

items: Checks 5, 6, 10 and 13. Monthly source slices partition identified MAU; do not sum MAU across months. Unidentified sessions excluded from MAU range from 2,286 to 3,703 per month, and are not unique people.
June to July signups: social 622 to 1,582 (+960), organic 1,305 to 453 (-852), search 700 to 417 (-283), unknown 26 to 25 (-1). These sum to -176, matching total 2,653 to 2,477 (check 14).

Extreme allocation of all unknowns to a single channel in either month bounds the social change at +934 to +985 and organic change at -878 to -827. Bounds are illustrative and do not allocate real users (check 14).

rows: H1: Unknown share is large / Rejected for signups
Around 1% each month; 238 of 24,000 total profiles (0.99%) have unknown source. This is not a guarantee of low error in every subgroup (checks 7, 10, 11).
H2: Missing labels can reverse the large July signup lead / Rejected for this example
Even assigning all 25 unknown signups to organic leaves a 1,104 lead for paid social. Close comparisons may behave differently (check 14).
H3: Source label establishes channel causality / Inconclusive
Source is first-touch and no click-level linkage is available; recorded labels may be wrong and confounding is untested. No causal lift or return on spend follows from these counts.

items: Bronze has 24,000 distinct users, 238 literal unknown values, no SQL NULLs or blanks; Silver matches Bronze source values for all profiles (checks 11-12). No flagged Silver profiles; 13 payment corrections appear in quality exceptions (checks 8-9).
Monthly new-payer unknown counts are 10, 1, 1, 1, 1 and 0; payer denominators can be small, making even one missing label consequential for close CAC comparisons (check 10).
Gold monthly spend has zero excluded days, but attribution is a channel-label match and cannot verify campaign or click attribution (check 5).
No independent validation of whether recorded known labels are correct; 1% unknown is not the total attribution error rate. Missingness may be systematic within segments.

The build-time registry SHA-256 (57b21d...1227) differs from this repository copy (4b5b2f...5554), although builder hashes match. Build checks do not demonstrate current definition equivalence or current source freshness.
Unknown users cannot be assigned without evidence. Sample comparisons are not a universal guarantee for every channel, cohort, period or metric.
Keep unknown visible, monitor source completeness by signup cohort, platform and campaign, and investigate collection failures.
For each decision, bound the result by allocating unknowns adversarially; require stronger evidence when rankings or cost ratios could flip.

Audit known source labels against independent attribution records and validate the build registry mismatch and fresh source fingerprints. Use experiments or a defensible causal design for spend decisions.
